# Harrowgate Community Trust

## Six-Month Programme Plan: January–June 2026

**Prepared for:** the Board of Trustees  
**Date:** January 2026  
**Programming budget:** £60,000  
**Status:** for approval

---

## 1. Summary

This is a portfolio plan, not a single bet. It does four things:

1. **Protects the one session that grew.** The Saturday family workshop is the only session that increased in 2025. It continues every Saturday, with family-fund childcare on 20 of the 26 Saturdays.
2. **Tests the transport explanation properly.** The evening film offer moves from Thursday to Friday, where the council's late bus will run from 6 February. Events end at 20:30, 45 minutes before the last bus at 21:15.
3. **Uses the east hall once it is safe to do so.** A soft reopening follows the commissioning certificate, then a four-week textile exhibition, *Threads of Harrowgate*, opens on 11 April.
4. **Keeps a small, honest Sunday test.** Four Sunday afternoon sessions test the one slot on which the trust has no local evidence, with a stop rule.

The core sessions are funded by the trust's £60,000 programming budget, not by a single external funder. The family fund only adds childcare; the bus is transport, not programme funding; the east hall repair is capital, not programming. If any one of those external supports falls away, the core programme still runs.

| Headline | Number |
|---|---:|
| Tuesday craft sessions | 25 |
| Thursday film matinees | 12 |
| Saturday family workshops | 26 |
| Friday evening events | 20 |
| East hall public workshops | 12 |
| Sunday trial sessions | 4 |
| Community-group minibus visits | 6 |
| Saturday family minibus runs | 6 |
| **Total budget, including contingency** | **£59,158** |
| **Headroom against £60,000** | **£842** |

**Key dates**

| Date | Milestone |
|---|---|
| Fri 6 Feb | Friday late bus starts; Friday evening series launches |
| Mon 9–Fri 27 Feb | East hall HVAC works; no public events in the east hall |
| Sat 28 Feb | Commissioning scheduled |
| Mon 2 Mar | Certificate check; east hall not booked before this |
| Sat 14 Mar | East hall soft reopening, subject to certificate |
| Sat 11 Apr–Sat 9 May | *Threads of Harrowgate* exhibition |
| Thu 30 Apr | Transport data pack to the town council's three-month review |
| Sat 20 Jun | Harrowgate Summer Assembly |
| Fri 10 Jul | Final evaluation report to the board |

---

## 2. What the evidence says

### 2.1 Attendance: a modest overall decline, but a clear mix shift

The attendance CSV is the only continuous quantitative series in the pack. It shows a 3.2% fall in total attendances in 2025 (1,030 to 997), but the fall is not uniform.

| Session | 2024 average per month | 2025 average per month | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Tuesday craft group | 33.9 | 29.2 | −14% |
| Thursday film club | 20.7 | 16.2 | −22% |
| Saturday family workshop | 31.2 | 37.8 | +21% |
| **All sessions** | **85.8** | **83.1** | **−3.2%** |

Two further points matter:

- **The decline is concentrated in the second half of 2025.** January–June 2025 totalled 523 attendances against 515 in the same months of 2024 (+1.6%). July–December 2025 totalled 474 against 515 (−8.0%).
- **The family workshop grew when childcare was added.** Its 2024 average was 26.9 in January–August and 42.3 in October–December, after the childcare pilot began.

The implication is not that the whole programme is failing. It is that the weekday and evening offer is losing people while the Saturday family offer is working. The plan therefore protects the family workshop and treats the weekday/evening offer as the part that needs testing.

### 2.2 The survey points to transport, but it is a stated preference

The 2025 member survey had 240 responses from 610 members (39%). It was self-selected, and the survey volunteer's method note is explicit: the evening-transport figure is a stated preference; people were asked to imagine a bus, not tested on whether they would come, and were not asked what they would pay.

| Survey question | Result |
|---|---|
| What stops you attending more often? (up to two) | Transport 61%; programme does not appeal 34%; cost 29%; caring responsibilities 27%; other 11% |
| Would you attend an evening event if transport were available? | Yes 44%; maybe 21%; no 35% |
| Which time suits you best? | Saturday morning 38%; weekday morning 24%; weekday evening 18%; Sunday afternoon 12%; no preference 8% |
| Would free childcare make it easier to attend? | Yes 27%, of whom 81% are members with children under 12 |

Transport is the strongest signal, but 35% say they would not come even with transport, and the 44% is not a forecast. The time-preference data is more useful for scheduling: Saturday morning is the strongest preference, weekday morning is next, and Sunday afternoon is the weakest. That is why the plan is weighted to Saturday morning and daytime, and why the Sunday test is deliberately small.

### 2.3 Prior interventions: remove friction, don't just change content

- **2023 Friday evening film pilot.** Three screenings drew 37, 23 and 19 people. Booking data shows 60 seats reserved for the first night and 48 for the second. The series was cancelled. The programmer's note says people liked the films but could not get home; staff interviews corroborate the 18:40 last bus and a £14 return taxi. This is a strong hypothesis, not proof.
- **2024 Saturday childcare pilot.** Attendance rose from an average of 27 in the first eight months of 2024 to 42 in the last four. The family fund paid £180 per session. Staff report that families stayed for the café and some began attending the Tuesday craft group. This is the clearest evidence in the pack that removing a practical barrier works.
- **2024 website and ticketing migration.** Web traffic rose 12%, but there is no evidence that attendance changed; the decline continued through 2025. Digital spend is therefore not treated as a solution.
- **2022 outreach van.** It averaged 11 attendances per visit, was withdrawn when its grant ended, and left no written evaluation. Staff remember it as "worthwhile but not a substitute for the building". It is not a model to scale.

### 2.4 Building and staffing constraints

- The east hall has not been climate-controlled since the HVAC unit failed in January 2025. The 2019 "climate-controlled" description is not relied on. The west hall and workshop room are usable throughout; the basement is damp and unsuitable for sensitive material.
- The trust has 2.0 FTE permanent staff (director, programmer), 0.5 FTE administrator and eight volunteers. Evening events require two staff present; childcare requires two qualified workers; volunteers are not asked to work alone after 18:00.
- Events may run until 23:00, and the building must be empty by 23:30.

The plan is built around these boundaries: no east hall public events before the certificate; no Thursday evening events; Friday events end at 20:30; sessional staff cover evenings; no new permanent posts.

### 2.5 What the January updates changed

| Update | What it says | How the plan changed |
|---|---|---|
| **Family fund** | £4,000 for January–June 2026, not the £9,000 in the seed pack. At £180 per Saturday, the fund covers at most 22 sessions (£3,960), leaving four Saturdays without family-fund support. The fund may also be used for other family support. From April, childcare must be advertised as "supported by the family fund", not permanently free. | I had assumed weekly childcare (26 × £180 = £4,680) was affordable. It is not. I have planned 20 sessions (£3,600) and held £400 for other family support, so six Saturdays run without childcare. The family workshop still runs every Saturday. From April, all materials use the "supported by the family fund" wording. |
| **East hall repair** | The council has approved the capital grant. The contractor works 9–27 February; commissioning is 28 February; the hall is expected to be usable for sensitive material from 1 March. The building officer says this is a plan, not a guarantee, and nothing should be booked before the commissioning certificate. The repair is capital and outside the £60,000. | I had treated the east hall as uncertain. I now plan a certificate check on 2 March, a soft reopening on 14 March and a textile exhibition from 11 April, with a fallback to the west hall or a later exhibition date. No east hall events are scheduled in January or February. The £18,000 repair is excluded from the programming budget. |
| **Transport** | The town council has approved a Friday late bus pilot from 6 February 2026. The last service from the square will leave at 21:15 instead of 18:40. It is funded for six months, covers Fridays only, and will be reviewed in July; the council will look at ridership after three months. There is no change to Saturday or Sunday service and no extra service on other weekdays. | I had assumed no viable evening offer. I now plan a Friday evening series ending at 20:30, and no Thursday evening events. I have not assumed late transport on any other day. The Friday series is a test, not a core commitment, and a data pack goes to the council by 30 April. |
| **Website** | The migration is complete, the old domain redirects, online booking works and the newsletter open rate is stable. The update says it has no effect on the programme plan. | No programme money is allocated to the website or to a digital campaign, and I have not assumed the 2024 traffic increase will translate into attendance. |

---

## 3. Month-by-month schedule

All events are in the west hall unless stated. Friday events run 18:30–20:30 and are staffed by two paid sessional staff from 17:00 to 21:00. The east hall is not used for public events until the commissioning certificate is issued.

### January 2026 — hold the core, prepare the test

- **Tuesdays 6, 13, 20, 27** — Craft Group, 10:00–12:00, workshop room.
- **Thursdays 8, 22** — Film Matinee, 14:00–16:00, west hall.
- **Saturdays 3, 10, 17, 24, 31** — Family Workshop, 10:00–12:00, west hall. Childcare on 10, 17, 24 and 31; 3 January runs without childcare.
- **No Friday evening events** — the late bus does not start until 6 February.
- **No east hall events** — the contractor is not yet on site, and the hall is not certified.
- **Behind the scenes:** confirm the 20-session family-fund request; book sessional staff and the curator; recruit workshop leaders and commissioned artists; set the attendance and box-office baseline; prepare the February launch marketing; order materials.
- **Family fund:** 4 sessions, £720.

### February 2026 — the Friday test launches; the east hall works

- **Tuesdays 3, 10, 17, 24** — Craft Group.
- **Thursdays 12, 26** — Film Matinee.
- **Saturdays 7, 14, 21, 28** — Family Workshop. Childcare on 7, 21 and 28; 14 February (start of half-term) runs without childcare.
- **Fridays 6, 13, 20, 27** — Friday Night, 18:30–20:30, west hall:
  - 6 February: launch film.
  - 13 February: talk.
  - 20 February: film.
  - 27 February: participatory talk/workshop.
- **East hall:** contractor on site 9–27 February. No public events. Commissioning scheduled for 28 February.
- **Saturday 28 February:** first family minibus run from the two estates.
- **Marketing:** Friday launch; half-term family offer.
- **Data:** count Friday attendance and bus use at every event; monthly check against the stop rule.
- **Family fund:** 3 sessions, £540.

### March 2026 — the east hall reopens, subject to certificate

- **Tuesdays 3, 10, 17, 24, 31** — Craft Group.
- **Thursdays 12, 26** — Film Matinee.
- **Saturdays 7, 14, 21, 28** — Family Workshop. Childcare on 7, 14 and 21; 28 March runs without childcare.
- **Fridays 6, 13, 20, 27** — Friday Night, west hall.
- **Monday 2 March:** certificate check. The east hall is not booked for any public event until the certificate is in hand.
- **Saturday 14 March, if certified:** East Hall Reopens, 11:00–15:00. Free entry; building tours, family textile activities and two workshop sessions. If the certificate is not issued, this moves to the west hall and the textile exhibition dates are reviewed.
- **From Monday 16 March:** exhibition install begins. Temperature and humidity are monitored for at least two weeks before any sensitive textile is installed. No sensitive material is stored in the basement.
- **Saturday 21 March:** family minibus run.
- **Marketing:** reopening; exhibition save-the-date.
- **Family fund:** 3 sessions, £540.

### April 2026 — the exhibition opens; Easter

- **Tuesdays 14, 21, 28** — Craft Group. No session on 7 April (Easter week).
- **Thursdays 9, 23** — Film Matinee.
- **Saturdays 4, 11, 18, 25** — Family Workshop. Childcare on 11, 18 and 25; 4 April (Easter Saturday) runs without childcare.
- **Fridays 10, 17, 24** — Friday Night, east hall, as the exhibition's late openings. No event on Good Friday, 3 April.
  - 10 April: film/preview.
  - 17 April: participatory talk.
  - 24 April: film.
- **East hall:** *Threads of Harrowgate* opens Saturday 11 April and runs to Saturday 9 May. Open Tuesday–Saturday, 10:00–16:00; the gallery stays open during the Friday events until 20:30. Public workshops: Wednesday 15, Saturday 18, Wednesday 22, Saturday 25, Wednesday 29 and Thursday 30 April (six sessions).
- **Community-group minibus visits:** Tuesday 14, Tuesday 21 and Tuesday 28 April.
- **Saturday 18 April:** family minibus run.
- **Marketing:** exhibition launch. From April, every childcare notice says "supported by the family fund" and does not describe childcare as permanently free.
- **Data:** transport data pack to the town council by Thursday 30 April, covering the first three months of the Friday bus.
- **Family fund:** 3 sessions, £540.

### May 2026 — the exhibition closes; the Sunday test begins

- **Tuesdays 5, 12, 19, 26** — Craft Group.
- **Thursdays 14, 28** — Film Matinee.
- **Saturdays 2, 9, 16, 23, 30** — Family Workshop. Childcare on 2, 9, 16 and 30; 23 May (half-term) runs without childcare.
- **Fridays 1, 8, 15, 22, 29** — Friday Night:
  - 1 May: talk, east hall.
  - 8 May: film and exhibition closing late, east hall.
  - 15 May: talk, west hall.
  - 22 May: film, west hall.
  - 29 May: participatory talk, west hall.
- **East hall:** exhibition through Saturday 9 May; closing event Friday 8 May; de-install Monday 11–Tuesday 12 May.
- **Sundays 17 and 31** — Sunday Afternoon trial, 14:00–16:00, west hall/café.
- **Community-group minibus visits:** Tuesday 5, Thursday 7 and Saturday 9 May.
- **Family minibus runs:** Saturday 2 and Saturday 30 May.
- **Marketing:** exhibition close; Sunday trial; half-term family offer.
- **Data:** review Friday bus ridership. If the average is below 20 per event or bus use is below 20%, June's Friday programme is reduced to monthly and the released sessional budget returns to contingency.
- **Family fund:** 4 sessions, £720.

### June 2026 — consolidate, celebrate, evaluate

- **Tuesdays 2, 9, 16, 23, 30** — Craft Group.
- **Thursdays 11, 25** — Film Matinee.
- **Saturdays 6, 13, 20, 27** — Family Workshop. Childcare on 6, 13 and 20; 27 June (end of term) runs without childcare.
- **Fridays 5, 12, 19, 26** — Friday Night, west hall.
- **Sundays 14 and 28** — Sunday Afternoon trial.
- **Saturday 20 June:** Family Workshop 10:00–12:00, then the Harrowgate Summer Assembly, 12:00–16:00, across the east hall, west hall and café. Commissioned works, local makers, performances and family activities. Childcare available.
- **Family minibus run:** Saturday 20 June.
- **No community-group minibus visit** — the exhibition has closed.
- **Evaluation:** attendance dashboard, pulse survey, six short interviews and a final report by Friday 10 July.
- **Marketing:** Summer Assembly; thank funders; no commitments beyond June.
- **Family fund:** 3 sessions, £540.

### How the plan answers the board's open questions

| Open question | What the plan does |
|---|---|
| Is the decline transport, programming or habits? | It tests transport with the Friday bus, adds new programming in the east hall and on Fridays, and measures both. It does not claim to settle "habits" in six months; the seasonal comparison will be part of the final report. |
| Would an evening series work now? | It tests Friday evenings, when the bus runs, rather than assuming the 2023 result is permanent. It does not run Thursday evenings, where there is no late transport. |
| Is the 2019 "climate-controlled" description safe? | No. The east hall is treated as uncontrolled until the 2026 commissioning certificate; textiles are installed only after monitoring. |
| Should childcare run every week? | No. The £4,000 fund covers at most 22 sessions; the plan delivers 20 and holds £400 for other family support. Six Saturdays run without childcare. |
| Is a Sunday series worth testing? | A four-session test with a stop rule, not a core commitment. The survey's 12% Sunday preference is the weakest signal, so the test is deliberately small. |
| How should success be measured? | Attendance per session, unique attendees, new member households, repeat attendance, bus use, family participation and income — not gross attendance alone. |

---

## 4. Budget

### 4.1 Budget by workstream

All unit costs are taken from `sources/spaces-and-costs.md`. Room hire is internal and has no fee. Permanent staff time is not charged to the programming budget; sessional and bought-in hours are.

#### A. Core programme — £18,900

---

## 5. Rationale

### 5.1 Which evidence I relied on

I treated the attendance CSV as the primary quantitative evidence because it is the only continuous series in the pack. It shows a 3.2% fall in total attendances in 2025, but the fall is not uniform: January–June 2025 was 1.6% above the same months of 2024, while July–December was 8.0% below; craft fell 14%, film fell 22%, and the Saturday family workshop grew 21%. That is why the plan protects the family workshop and treats the weekday and evening offer as the part that needs testing, rather than assuming a general collapse.

I used the 2025 member survey as a signal, not a forecast. Transport is the most cited barrier at 61%, but the 44% who said they would attend an evening event if transport were available were answering a hypothetical question; the survey volunteer explicitly warns that the trust did not test whether they would actually come or what they would pay. I therefore did not plan on 44% turning up. I used the time-preference data — Saturday morning 38%, weekday morning 24%, weekday evening 18%, Sunday afternoon 12% — to weight the programme toward Saturday morning and daytime, and to keep the Sunday test small.

I used the prior interventions as natural experiments. The 2023 Friday films drew 37, 23 and 19 people, with 60 and 48 seats reserved, and were cancelled because people could not get home; the staff interviews corroborate the 18:40 last bus and the £14 return taxi. That is a strong hypothesis, not proof, so the Friday series is a test with a stop rule. The 2024 childcare pilot, where the family workshop average rose from 27 to 42, is the clearest evidence that removing a practical barrier works; it is why childcare remains central to the family offer, within the reduced fund. The 2024 website migration produced a 12% traffic increase but no attendance change, which is why no programme money is going into digital. The 2022 van averaged 11 attendances per visit and left no evaluation, which is why the plan does not scale outreach; the minibus brings groups to the building instead.

I treated the constraints as hard boundaries, not preferences: the east hall is unavailable until the certificate; volunteers are not alone after 18:00; evening events need two staff; childcare needs two qualified workers; the licence runs to 23:00 and the building must be empty by 23:30. The plan is built around those boundaries.

### 5.2 How the January updates changed my assumptions

**Family fund.** The seed pack said £9,000; the 12 January update says £4,000. I had assumed that weekly childcare — 26 sessions at £180, or £4,680 — was affordable. It is not. The fund covers at most 22 sessions (£3,960). I have planned 20 sessions (£3,600), held £400 for other family support, and built in six Saturdays without childcare. The family offer therefore changes from "childcare every week" to "childcare on 20 of 26 Saturdays, with the workshop still running every week". From April, the wording changes to "supported by the family fund". This is a material change: the family workshop remains the core, but childcare is now a limited enhancement rather than a weekly guarantee.

**East hall repair.** The seed pack said the repair depended on a grant application and might be complete in late February. The update confirms the grant, the works dates (9–27 February), commissioning on 28 February and expected usability from 1 March. But the building officer says this is a plan, not a guarantee, and nothing should be booked before the commissioning certificate. I therefore did not schedule any east hall public events in January or February. I put the certificate check on 2 March, a soft reopening on 14 March and the sensitive textile exhibition on 11 April, with a fallback to the west hall or a later date. The east hall changes from "maybe" to "planned, but gated".

**Transport.** The seed pack said the last bus was 18:40 and the 2023 films failed. The update adds a Friday late bus from 6 February, last service 21:15, Fridays only, for six months, with a review in July and a ridership check after three months. I changed the evening plan from "no evening offer" to a Friday series ending at 20:30, and kept Thursday evenings off. I did not extend the assumption to other weekdays, and I did not make core sessions depend on the bus. I added a 30 April data pack to feed the council's three-month review. The Friday series is therefore both a programme and an evidence-gathering exercise.

**Website.** The update says the migration is complete, online booking works and there is no programme effect. I have not allocated programme money to the website or a digital campaign, and I have not assumed that the 2024 traffic increase will translate into attendance.

### 5.3 What I am uncertain about

| Uncertainty | Why it matters | How the plan responds |
|---|---|---|
| **The cause of the decline** — transport, programming or changed habits | If transport is not the binding constraint, the Friday series may underperform; if programming is the issue, the east hall season may not be enough | The plan tests transport (Friday bus), adds programming (east hall, Friday talks, Sunday trial) and measures both. It does not claim to settle habits in six months; the final report will compare like-for-like months and report the limits of the evidence. |
| **The survey's stated preference** | 44% "yes" may not convert into attendance | The plan targets 25 per Friday event, not 44%; it counts actual attendance and bus use, and reports both to the board and the council. |
| **The bus pilot's continuation** | If the council does not continue the bus after July, the Friday model may not survive | The plan covers January–June only and makes no July commitments. The Friday series is not a core session. If the bus ends, the remaining films can move to a Saturday afternoon or an early Friday slot, and the core still runs. |
| **The HVAC certificate date and environmental stability** | The textile exhibition could be delayed, or the hall could be certified but not stable enough for sensitive material | The certificate is a gate, not an assumption. Temperature and humidity are monitored for at least two weeks before install; the curator signs off. If the hall is not ready, the exhibition moves later or to a non-sensitive format in the west hall. No textiles are stored in the basement. |
| **The family fund trustees' decision** | The £400 balance may be used elsewhere; the 20 sessions are a request, not a guarantee | Six no-childcare Saturdays are built into the schedule; the family workshop still runs. If the fund is reduced, childcare is reduced first, not the workshop. If 22 sessions are confirmed, two dates are restored. |
| **Attendance and materials estimates** | Craft 9, family 10, exhibition 350, Summer 150 and the other material counts are assumptions | The £5,378 contingency is the first call. Materials can be trimmed without cancelling sessions; attendance is reviewed weekly. |
| **Staff and volunteer capacity** | 2.0 FTE plus 0.5 FTE is a small team for a weekly Friday and Saturday programme | Friday evenings use two paid sessional staff; no new permanent posts are created; volunteers are never alone after 18:00. If the rota becomes unsafe, Friday frequency is reduced before core sessions. |
| **Income** | Ticket and café income may be lower than the indicative targets | The budget is gross and does not depend on income. Income is monitored monthly and reported separately. |
| **Seasonality and weather** | January and February are low months; summer half-term and the end of term affect families | Childcare-free Saturdays are placed on likely low dates (post-Christmas, half-term, Easter, end of term); the family minibus runs on selected dates; the final report compares with the same months in 2025. |
| **The east hall repair's quality** | "Usable" may not mean stable enough for textiles | The building officer's certificate is necessary but not sufficient; the curator's environmental monitoring is the second gate. |

### 5.4 Why this mix, not a single bet

The board has three explanations and no decision. The evidence does not justify betting the whole £60,000 on one of them. The plan weights the budget toward what is already working (core and family, £18,900), a controlled transport test (Friday, £10,200), a signature programming season (east hall, £10,500, plus commissions and the Summer Assembly), and a small Sunday test (£1,900). Access transport, marketing and evaluation make up the rest.

The core is funded by the trust's programming budget, not a single external funder. The family fund only adds childcare; the bus is transport, not programme funding; the east hall repair is capital, not programming. If the Friday test fails, the core still runs. If the family fund is cut, the workshop still runs. If the east hall certificate slips, the west hall programme still runs. That is the point of the portfolio: it gives the board evidence without putting the core programme at risk.

---

## 6. How we will know whether it is working

The board's sixth open question is how to measure success. Gross attendance alone would reward activity rather than reach, so the plan uses a small dashboard.

| Measure | Baseline | Target or decision rule |
|---|---|---|
| **Craft group attendance per session** | 2025 January–June average: 30.5 per month | 32 per month by June |
| **Film matinee attendance** | New format; Thursday evening 2025 average 17 per month | 20 per screening by June; if below 12 for three consecutive screenings, fold into Friday |
| **Family workshop attendance** | 2025 January–June average: 39.7 per month | 45 per month by June; childcare delivered on 20 dates |
| **Friday attendance** | New | 25 per event average; 30% arriving by bus; if below 20 per event or below 20% bus use after three months, reduce June to monthly |
| **East hall exhibition** | New | 500 visitors and 350 workshop participants; curator environmental sign-off before install |
| **Sunday trial** | New; survey preference 12% | 20 per session; if below 15 for two consecutive sessions, cancel the remaining two |
| **New member households** | 610 members | 60 new households by June |
| **Repeat attendance** | Not currently measured | 25% of Friday and Sunday attenders return at least once |
| **Income** | Not assumed | £7,000 indicative across tickets, workshops and café; reported, not relied on |
| **Access** | 6 group visits; 6 family minibus runs | At least 8 passengers per minibus run; if below 8 for three runs, stop and reallocate |
| **Staffing and licensing** | Current arrangements | Two paid staff at every evening event; no volunteer alone after 18:00; building empty by 23:30 |

**Reporting**

- **Monthly:** a one-page dashboard to the director and treasurer: attendance, income, bus counts, materials spend and any staffing issues.
- **End March:** a short board update on the Friday launch, the east hall certificate and the family-fund position.
- **30 April:** the transport data pack to the town council for its three-month review.
- **10 July:** the final evaluation report: what worked, what did not, what the board should continue, change or stop.

---

## 7. Approval requested

The board is asked to:

1. **Approve the programme and the budget of £59,158**, within the £60,000 ceiling, including the £5,378 contingency.
2. **Confirm the family-fund request** of 20 sessions at £180 (£3,600), with £400 held for other family support. If the trustees prefer to commit 22 sessions, the plan will restore childcare on 14 February and 28 March.
3. **Note the east hall certificate gate.** No east hall public event will be booked before the commissioning certificate; the 14 March soft opening and the 11 April exhibition are contingent on it.
4. **Agree the stop rules** for the Friday series, the Sunday trial and the minibus runs, so that underused activity can be stopped and the budget returned to contingency without a further board decision.
5. **Agree the evaluation framework and reporting dates**, including the 30 April transport data pack and the 10 July final report.

# Harrowgate Community Trust

## Six-Month Programme Plan: January–June 2026

**Prepared for:** the Board of Trustees  
**Date:** January 2026  
**Programming budget:** £60,000  
**Status:** for approval

---

## 1. Summary

This is a portfolio plan, not a single bet. It does four things:

1. **Protects the one session that grew.** The Saturday family workshop is the only session that increased in 2025. It continues every Saturday, with family-fund childcare on 20 of the 26 Saturdays.
2. **Tests the transport explanation properly.** The evening film offer moves from Thursday to Friday, where the council's late bus will run from 6 February. Events end at 20:30, 45 minutes before the last bus at 21:15.
3. **Uses the east hall once it is safe to do so.** A soft reopening follows the commissioning certificate, then a four-week textile exhibition, *Threads of Harrowgate*, opens on 11 April.
4. **Keeps a small, honest Sunday test.** Four Sunday afternoon sessions test the one slot on which the trust has no local evidence, with a stop rule.

The core sessions are funded by the trust's £60,000 programming budget, not by a single external funder. The family fund only adds childcare; the bus is transport, not programme funding; the east hall repair is capital, not programming. If any one of those external supports falls away, the core programme still runs.

| Headline | Number |
|---|---:|
| Tuesday craft sessions | 25 |
| Thursday film matinees | 12 |
| Saturday family workshops | 26 |
| Friday evening events | 20 |
| East hall public workshops | 12 |
| Sunday trial sessions | 4 |
| Community-group minibus visits | 6 |
| Saturday family minibus runs | 6 |
| **Total budget, including contingency** | **£59,158** |
| **Headroom against £60,000** | **£842** |

**Key dates**

| Date | Milestone |
|---|---|
| Fri 6 Feb | Friday late bus starts; Friday evening series launches |
| Mon 9–Fri 27 Feb | East hall HVAC works; no public events in the east hall |
| Sat 28 Feb | Commissioning scheduled |
| Mon 2 Mar | Certificate check; east hall not booked before this |
| Sat 14 Mar | East hall soft reopening, subject to certificate |
| Sat 11 Apr–Sat 9 May | *Threads of Harrowgate* exhibition |
| Thu 30 Apr | Transport data pack to the town council's three-month review |
| Sat 20 Jun | Harrowgate Summer Assembly |
| Fri 10 Jul | Final evaluation report to the board |

---

## 2. What the evidence says

### 2.1 Attendance: a modest overall decline, but a clear mix shift

The attendance CSV is the only continuous quantitative series in the pack. It shows a 3.2% fall in total attendances in 2025 (1,030 to 997), but the fall is not uniform.

| Session | 2024 average per month | 2025 average per month | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Tuesday craft group | 33.9 | 29.2 | −14% |
| Thursday film club | 20.7 | 16.2 | −22% |
| Saturday family workshop | 31.2 | 37.8 | +21% |
| **All sessions** | **85.8** | **83.1** | **−3.2%** |

Two further points matter:

- **The decline is concentrated in the second half of 2025.** January–June 2025 totalled 523 attendances against 515 in the same months of 2024 (+1.6%). July–December 2025 totalled 474 against 515 (−8.0%).
- **The family workshop grew when childcare was added.** Its 2024 average was 26.9 in January–August and 42.3 in October–December, after the childcare pilot began.

The implication is not that the whole programme is failing. It is that the weekday and evening offer is losing people while the Saturday family offer is working. The plan therefore protects the family workshop and treats the weekday/evening offer as the part that needs testing.

### 2.2 The survey points to transport, but it is a stated preference

The 2025 member survey had 240 responses from 610 members (39%). It was self-selected, and the survey volunteer's method note is explicit: the evening-transport figure is a stated preference; people were asked to imagine a bus, not tested on whether they would come, and were not asked what they would pay.

| Survey question | Result |
|---|---|
| What stops you attending more often? (up to two) | Transport 61%; programme does not appeal 34%; cost 29%; caring responsibilities 27%; other 11% |
| Would you attend an evening event if transport were available? | Yes 44%; maybe 21%; no 35% |
| Which time suits you best? | Saturday morning 38%; weekday morning 24%; weekday evening 18%; Sunday afternoon 12%; no preference 8% |
| Would free childcare make it easier to attend? | Yes 27%, of whom 81% are members with children under 12 |

Transport is the strongest signal, but 35% say they would not come even with transport, and the 44% is not a forecast. The time-preference data is more useful for scheduling: Saturday morning is the strongest preference, weekday morning is next, and Sunday afternoon is the weakest. That is why the plan is weighted to Saturday morning and daytime, and why the Sunday test is deliberately small.

### 2.3 Prior interventions: remove friction, don't just change content

- **2023 Friday evening film pilot.** Three screenings drew 37, 23 and 19 people. Booking data shows 60 seats reserved for the first night and 48 for the second. The series was cancelled. The programmer's note says people liked the films but could not get home; staff interviews corroborate the 18:40 last bus and a £14 return taxi. This is a strong hypothesis, not proof.
- **2024 Saturday childcare pilot.** Attendance rose from an average of 27 in the first eight months of 2024 to 42 in the last four. The family fund paid £180 per session. Staff report that families stayed for the café and some began attending the Tuesday craft group. This is the clearest evidence in the pack that removing a practical barrier works.
- **2024 website and ticketing migration.** Web traffic rose 12%, but there is no evidence that attendance changed; the decline continued through 2025. Digital spend is therefore not treated as a solution.
- **2022 outreach van.** It averaged 11 attendances per visit, was withdrawn when its grant ended, and left no written evaluation. Staff remember it as "worthwhile but not a substitute for the building". It is not a model to scale.

### 2.4 Building and staffing constraints

- The east hall has not been climate-controlled since the HVAC unit failed in January 2025. The 2019 "climate-controlled" description is not relied on. The west hall and workshop room are usable throughout; the basement is damp and unsuitable for sensitive material.
- The trust has 2.0 FTE permanent staff (director, programmer), 0.5 FTE administrator and eight volunteers. Evening events require two staff present; childcare requires two qualified workers; volunteers are not asked to work alone after 18:00.
- Events may run until 23:00, and the building must be empty by 23:30.

The plan is built around these boundaries: no east hall public events before the certificate; no Thursday evening events; Friday events end at 20:30; sessional staff cover evenings; no new permanent posts.

### 2.5 What the January updates changed

| Update | What it says | How the plan changed |
|---|---|---|
| **Family fund** | £4,000 for January–June 2026, not the £9,000 in the seed pack. At £180 per Saturday, the fund covers at most 22 sessions (£3,960), leaving four Saturdays without family-fund support. The fund may also be used for other family support. From April, childcare must be advertised as "supported by the family fund", not permanently free. | I had assumed weekly childcare (26 × £180 = £4,680) was affordable. It is not. I have planned 20 sessions (£3,600) and held £400 for other family support, so six Saturdays run without childcare. The family workshop still runs every Saturday. From April, all materials use the "supported by the family fund" wording. |
| **East hall repair** | The council has approved the capital grant. The contractor works 9–27 February; commissioning is 28 February; the hall is expected to be usable for sensitive material from 1 March. The building officer says this is a plan, not a guarantee, and nothing should be booked before the commissioning certificate. The repair is capital and outside the £60,000. | I had treated the east hall as uncertain. I now plan a certificate check on 2 March, a soft reopening on 14 March and a textile exhibition from 11 April, with a fallback to the west hall or a later exhibition date. No east hall events are scheduled in January or February. The £18,000 repair is excluded from the programming budget. |
| **Transport** | The town council has approved a Friday late bus pilot from 6 February 2026. The last service from the square will leave at 21:15 instead of 18:40. It is funded for six months, covers Fridays only, and will be reviewed in July; the council will look at ridership after three months. There is no change to Saturday or Sunday service and no extra service on other weekdays. | I had assumed no viable evening offer. I now plan a Friday evening series ending at 20:30, and no Thursday evening events. I have not assumed late transport on any other day. The Friday series is a test, not a core commitment, and a data pack goes to the council by 30 April. |
| **Website** | The migration is complete, the old domain redirects, online booking works and the newsletter open rate is stable. The update says it has no effect on the programme plan. | No programme money is allocated to the website or to a digital campaign, and I have not assumed the 2024 traffic increase will translate into attendance. |

---

## 3. Month-by-month schedule

All events are in the west hall unless stated. Friday events run 18:30–20:30 and are staffed by two paid sessional staff from 17:00 to 21:00. The east hall is not used for public events until the commissioning certificate is issued.

### January 2026 — hold the core, prepare the test

- **Tuesdays 6, 13, 20, 27** — Craft Group, 10:00–12:00, workshop room.
- **Thursdays 8, 22** — Film Matinee, 14:00–16:00, west hall.
- **Saturdays 3, 10, 17, 24, 31** — Family Workshop, 10:00–12:00, west hall. Childcare on 10, 17, 24 and 31; 3 January runs without childcare.
- **No Friday evening events** — the late bus does not start until 6 February.
- **No east hall events** — the contractor is not yet on site, and the hall is not certified.
- **Behind the scenes:** confirm the 20-session family-fund request; book sessional staff and the curator; recruit workshop leaders and commissioned artists; set the attendance and box-office baseline; prepare the February launch marketing; order materials.
- **Family fund:** 4 sessions, £720.

### February 2026 — the Friday test launches; the east hall works

- **Tuesdays 3, 10, 17, 24** — Craft Group.
- **Thursdays 12, 26** — Film Matinee.
- **Saturdays 7, 14, 21, 28** — Family Workshop. Childcare on 7, 21 and 28; 14 February (start of half-term) runs without childcare.
- **Fridays 6, 13, 20, 27** — Friday Night, 18:30–20:30, west hall:
  - 6 February: launch film.
  - 13 February: talk.
  - 20 February: film.
  - 27 February: participatory talk/workshop.
- **East hall:** contractor on site 9–27 February. No public events. Commissioning scheduled for 28 February.
- **Saturday 28 February:** first family minibus run from the two estates.
- **Marketing:** Friday launch; half-term family offer.
- **Data:** count Friday attendance and bus use at every event; monthly check against the stop rule.
- **Family fund:** 3 sessions, £540.

### March 2026 — the east hall reopens, subject to certificate

- **Tuesdays 3, 10, 17, 24, 31** — Craft Group.

- **Fridays 6, 13, 20, 27** — Friday Night, west hall.
- **Monday 2 March:** certificate check. The east hall is not booked for any public event until the certificate is in hand.
- **Saturday 14 March, if certified:** East Hall Reopens, 11:00–15:00. Free entry; building tours, family textile activities and two workshop sessions. If the certificate is not issued, this moves to the west hall and the textile exhibition dates are reviewed.
- **From Monday 16 March:** exhibition install begins. Temperature and humidity are monitored for at least two weeks before any sensitive textile is installed. No sensitive material is stored in the basement.

### April 2026 — the exhibition opens; Easter

- **Fridays 10, 17, 24** — Friday Night, east hall, as the exhibition's late openings. No event on Good Friday, 3 April.
  - 10 April: film/preview.

  - 24 April: film.
- **East hall:** *Threads of Harrowgate* opens Saturday 11 April and runs to Saturday 9 May. Open Tuesday–Saturday, 10:00–16:00; the gallery stays open during the Friday events until 20:30. Public workshops: Wednesday 15, Saturday 18, Wednesday 22, Saturday 25, Wednesday 29 and Thursday 30 April (six sessions).
- **Community-group minibus visits:** Tuesday 14, Tuesday 21 and Tuesday 28 April.

- **Marketing:** exhibition launch. From April, every childcare notice says "supported by the family fund" and does not describe childcare as permanently free.

- **Family fund:** 3 sessions, £540.

### May 2026 — the exhibition closes; the Sunday test begins

- **Tuesdays 5, 12, 19, 26** — Craft Group.

- **Fridays 1, 8, 15, 22, 29** — Friday Night:

  - 29 May: participatory talk, west hall.
- **East hall:** exhibition through Saturday 9 May; closing event Friday 8 May; de-install Monday 11–Tuesday 12 May.
- **Sundays 17 and 31** — Sunday Afternoon trial, 14:00–16:00, west hall/café.
- **Community-group minibus visits:** Tuesday 5, Thursday 7 and Saturday 9 May.
- **Family minibus runs:** Saturday 2 and Saturday 30 May.
- **Marketing:** exhibition close; Sunday trial; half-term family offer.
- **Data:** review Friday bus ridership. If the average is below 20 per event or bus use is below 20%, June's Friday programme is reduced to monthly and the released sessional budget returns to contingency.
- **Family fund:** 4 sessions, £720.

### June 2026 — consolidate, celebrate, evaluate

- **Tuesdays 2, 9, 16, 23, 30** — Craft Group.
- **Thursdays 11, 25** — Film Matinee.
- **Saturdays 6, 13, 20, 27** — Family Workshop. Childcare on 6, 13 and 20; 27 June (end of term) runs without childcare.
- **Fridays 5, 12, 19, 26** — Friday Night, west hall.

- **Family minibus run:** Saturday 20 June.
- **No community-group minibus visit** — the exhibition has closed.
- **Evaluation:** attendance dashboard, pulse survey, six short interviews and a final report by Friday 10 July.
- **Marketing:** Summer Assembly; thank funders; no commitments beyond June.
- **Family fund:** 3 sessions, £540.

### How the plan answers the board's open questions

| Open question | What the plan does |

| How should success be measured? | Attendance per session, unique attendees, new member households, repeat attendance, bus use, family participation and income — not gross attendance alone. |

- **Marketing:** £600 per month core, plus £1,200 for the exhibition and £600 for the Summer Assembly.
- **No VAT, no capital, no family fund** is included in the £60,000 table.
- **Contingency:** 10% of direct costs. If it is insufficient, the first savings are reducing Friday frequency, then reducing commissions; core sessions and childcare are protected.

---

## 5. Rationale

### 5.1 Which evidence I relied on

I treated the attendance CSV as the primary quantitative evidence because it is the only continuous series in the pack. It shows a 3.2% fall in total attendances in 2025, but the fall is not uniform: January–June 2025 was 1.6% above the same months of 2024, while July–December was 8.0% below; craft fell 14%, film fell 22%, and the Saturday family workshop grew 21%. That is why the plan protects the family workshop and treats the weekday and evening offer as the part that needs testing, rather than assuming a general collapse.

I used the 2025 member survey as a signal, not a forecast. Transport is the most cited barrier at 61%, but the 44% who said they would attend an evening event if transport were available were answering a hypothetical question; the survey volunteer explicitly warns that the trust did not test whether they would actually come or what they would pay. I therefore did not plan on 44% turning up. I used the time-preference data — Saturday morning 38%, weekday morning 24%, weekday evening 18%, Sunday afternoon 12% — to weight the programme toward Saturday morning and daytime, and to keep the Sunday test small.

I used the prior interventions as natural experiments. The 2023 Friday films drew 37, 23 and 19 people, with 60 and 48 seats reserved, and were cancelled because people could not get home; the staff interviews corroborate the 18:40 last bus and the £14 return taxi. That is a strong hypothesis, not proof, so the Friday series is a test with a stop rule. The 2024 childcare pilot, where the family workshop average rose from 27 to 42, is the clearest evidence that removing a practical barrier works; it is why childcare remains central to the family offer, within the reduced fund. The 2024 website migration produced a 12% traffic increase but no attendance change, which is why no programme money is going into digital. The 2022 van averaged 11 attendances per visit and left no evaluation, which is why the plan does not scale outreach; the minibus brings groups to the building instead.

I treated the constraints as hard boundaries, not preferences: the east hall is unavailable until the certificate; volunteers are not alone after 18:00; evening events need two staff; childcare needs two qualified workers; the licence runs to 23:00 and the building must be empty by 23:30. The plan is built around those boundaries.

### 5.2 How the January updates changed my assumptions

**Family fund.** The seed pack said £9,000; the 12 January update says £4,000. I had assumed that weekly childcare — 26 sessions at £180, or £4,680 — was affordable. It is not. The fund covers at most 22 sessions (£3,960). I have planned 20 sessions (£3,600), held £400 for other family support, and built in six Saturdays without childcare. The family offer therefore changes from "childcare every week" to "childcare on 20 of 26 Saturdays, with the workshop still running every week". From April, the wording changes to "supported by the family fund". This is a material change: the family workshop remains the core, but childcare is now a limited enhancement rather than a weekly guarantee.

**East hall repair.** The seed pack said the repair depended on a grant application and might be complete in late February. The update confirms the grant, the works dates (9–27 February), commissioning on 28 February and expected usability from 1 March. But the building officer says this is a plan, not a guarantee, and nothing should be booked before the commissioning certificate. I therefore did not schedule any east hall public events in January or February. I put the certificate check on 2 March, a soft reopening on 14 March and the sensitive textile exhibition on 11 April, with a fallback to the west hall or a later date. The east hall changes from "maybe" to "planned, but gated".

**Transport.** The seed pack said the last bus was 18:40 and the 2023 films failed. The update adds a Friday late bus from 6 February, last service 21:15, Fridays only, for six months, with a review in July and a ridership check after three months. I changed the evening plan from "no evening offer" to a Friday series ending at 20:30, and kept Thursday evenings off. I did not extend the assumption to other weekdays, and I did not make core sessions depend on the bus. I added a 30 April data pack to feed the council's three-month review. The Friday series is therefore both a programme and an evidence-gathering exercise.

**Website.** The update says the migration is complete, online booking works and there is no programme effect. I have not allocated programme money to the website or a digital campaign, and I have not assumed that the 2024 traffic increase will translate into attendance.

### 5.3 What I am uncertain about

| Uncertainty | Why it matters | How the plan responds |
|---|---|---|
| **The cause of the decline** — transport, programming or changed habits | If transport is not the binding constraint, the Friday series may underperform; if programming is the issue, the east hall season may not be enough | The plan tests transport (Friday bus), adds programming (east hall, Friday talks, Sunday trial) and measures both. It does not claim to settle habits in six months; the final report will compare like-for-like months and report the limits of the evidence. |
| **The survey's stated preference** | 44% "yes" may not convert into attendance | The plan targets 25 per Friday event, not 44%; it counts actual attendance and bus use, and reports both to the board and the council. |
| **The bus pilot's continuation** | If the council does not continue the bus after July, the Friday model may not survive | The plan covers January–June only and makes no July commitments. The Friday series is not a core session. If the bus ends, the remaining films can move to a Saturday afternoon or an early Friday slot, and the core still runs. |
| **The HVAC certificate date and environmental stability** | The textile exhibition could be delayed, or the hall could be certified but not stable enough for sensitive material | The certificate is a gate, not an assumption. Temperature and humidity are monitored for at least two weeks before install; the curator signs off. If the hall is not ready, the exhibition moves later or to a non-sensitive format in the west hall. No textiles are stored in the basement. |
| **The family fund trustees' decision** | The £400 balance may be used elsewhere; the 20 sessions are a request, not a guarantee | Six no-childcare Saturdays are built into the schedule; the family workshop still runs. If the fund is reduced, childcare is reduced first, not the workshop. If 22 sessions are confirmed, two dates are restored. |
| **Attendance and materials estimates** | Craft 9, family 10, exhibition 350, Summer 150 and the other material counts are assumptions | The £5,378 contingency is the first call. Materials can be trimmed without cancelling sessions; attendance is reviewed weekly. |
| **Staff and volunteer capacity** | 2.0 FTE plus 0.5 FTE is a small team for a weekly Friday and Saturday programme | Friday evenings use two paid sessional staff; no new permanent posts are created; volunteers are never alone after 18:00. If the rota becomes unsafe, Friday frequency is reduced before core sessions. |
| **Income** | Ticket and café income may be lower than the indicative targets | The budget is gross and does not depend on income. Income is monitored monthly and reported separately. |
| **Seasonality and weather** | January and February are low months; summer half-term and the end of term affect families | Childcare-free Saturdays are placed on likely low dates (post-Christmas, half-term, Easter, end of term); the family minibus runs on selected dates; the final report compares with the same months in 2025. |
| **The east hall repair's quality** | "Usable" may not mean stable enough for textiles | The building officer's certificate is necessary but not sufficient; the curator's environmental monitoring is the second gate. |

### 5.4 Why this mix, not a single bet

The board has three explanations and no decision. The evidence does not justify betting the whole £60,000 on one of them. The plan weights the budget toward what is already working (core and family, £18,900), a controlled transport test (Friday, £10,200), a signature programming season (east hall, £10,500, plus commissions and the Summer Assembly), and a small Sunday test (£1,900). Access transport, marketing and evaluation make up the rest.

The core is funded by the trust's programming budget, not a single external funder. The family fund only adds childcare; the bus is transport, not programme funding; the east hall repair is capital, not programming. If the Friday test fails, the core still runs. If the family fund is cut, the workshop still runs. If the east hall certificate slips, the west hall programme still runs. That is the point of the portfolio: it gives the board evidence without putting the core programme at risk.

---

## 6. How we will know whether it is working

The board's sixth open question is how to measure success. Gross attendance alone would reward activity rather than reach, so the plan uses a small dashboard.

| Measure | Baseline | Target or decision rule |
|---|---|---|
| **Craft group attendance per session** | 2025 January–June average: 30.5 per month | 32 per month by June |
| **Film matinee attendance** | New format; Thursday evening 2025 average 17 per month | 20 per screening by June; if below 12 for three consecutive screenings, fold into Friday |
| **Family workshop attendance** | 2025 January–June average: 39.7 per month | 45 per month by June; childcare delivered on 20 dates |
| **Friday attendance** | New | 25 per event average; 30% arriving by bus; if below 20 per event or below 20% bus use after three months, reduce June to monthly |
| **East hall exhibition** | New | 500 visitors and 350 workshop participants; curator environmental sign-off before install |
| **Sunday trial** | New; survey preference 12% | 20 per session; if below 15 for two consecutive sessions, cancel the remaining two |
| **New member households** | 610 members | 60 new households by June |
| **Repeat attendance** | Not currently measured | 25% of Friday and Sunday attenders return at least once |
| **Income** | Not assumed | £7,000 indicative across tickets, workshops and café; reported, not relied on |
| **Access** | 6 group visits; 6 family minibus runs | At least 8 passengers per minibus run; if below 8 for three runs, stop and reallocate |
| **Staffing and licensing** | Current arrangements | Two paid staff at every evening event; no volunteer alone after 18:00; building empty by 23:30 |

**Reporting**

- **Monthly:** a one-page dashboard to the director and treasurer: attendance, income, bus counts, materials spend and any staffing issues.
- **End March:** a short board update on the Friday launch, the east hall certificate and the family-fund position.
- **30 April:** the transport data pack to the town council for its three-month review.
- **10 July:** the final evaluation report: what worked, what did not, what the board should continue, change or stop.

---

## 7. Approval requested

The board is asked to:

1. **Approve the programme and the budget of £59,158**, within the £60,000 ceiling, including the £5,378 contingency.
2. **Confirm the family-fund request** of 20 sessions at £180 (£3,600), with £400 held for other family support. If the trustees prefer to commit 22 sessions, the plan will restore childcare on 14 February and 28 March.
3. **Note the east hall certificate gate.** No east hall public event will be booked before the commissioning certificate; the 14 March soft opening and the 11 April exhibition are contingent on it.
4. **Agree the stop rules** for the Friday series, the Sunday trial and the minibus runs, so that underused activity can be stopped and the budget returned to contingency without a further board decision.
5. **Agree the evaluation framework and reporting dates**, including the 30 April transport data pack and the 10 July final report.

python3 - <<'PY'
import re
text=open('deliverables/plan.md',encoding='utf-8').read()
# Extract budget line item rows (3 columns, last numeric) and section headers
sec=text[text.index('#### A. Core programme'):text.index('### 4.2 Budget summary')]
sections=re.split(r'\n#### ',sec)[1:]
total=0
for s in sections:
    header=s.splitlines()[0]
    declared=int(re.search(r'£([\d,]+)',header).group(1).replace(',',''))
    rows=[]
    for line in s.splitlines():
        if line.strip().startswith('|') and '---' not in line:
            cells=[c.strip() for c in line.strip().strip('|').split('|')]
            if len(cells)==3 and re.fullmatch(r'[\d,]+',cells[2]):
                rows.append(int(cells[2].replace(',','')))
    # rows includes line items and maybe subtotal if numeric (bold not matched)
    print(header, 'declared', declared, 'rows', rows, 'sum', sum(rows))
    total += sum(rows)
print('TOTAL', total)
print('Contingency', total*0.10, 'Grand', total*1.10)
# monthly
ms=re.search(r'### 4.3 Monthly cash flow(.*?)### 4.4',text,re.S).group(1)
months=re.findall(r'\|\s*(January|February|March|April|May|June)\s*\|\s*([\d,]+)\s*\|',ms)
print('monthly sum', sum(int(v.replace(',','')) for m,v in months), months)
PY
